sentences.text: M/s Central Coalfields Limited, a subsidiary company of Coal India Limited through the Chairman-cum-Managing Director, Ranchi 2.
The Chairman-cum-Managing Director, Central Coalfields Limited, Ranchi 3.
The Managing Director, Land Revenue, Central Coalfields Limited, Ranchi 4.
The Project Officer, Govindpur Project, Kathara Area, Bokaro Thermal, Bokaro 5.
Respondents CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH SHANKAR For the Petitioner : Mr. Kumar Sundaram, Advocate For the Resp
Mr. Prashant Pallav, D.S.G.I. Mr. Tauseef Jawed, A.C. to D.S.G.I. Mrs. Niki Sinha, C.G.C.

For the Resp. No. 5 : Mr. Sudhanshu Kumar Singh, A.C. to S.C.-III Order No. 06 Dated: 14.09.2023 The present writ petition has been filed for following reliefs:
(i) For issuance of direction upon the respondent-Central Coalfields Ltd. (CCL) to grant appropriate compensation to the petitioner in terms with the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short, "the Act, 2013") for acquisition of piece of land in the year 1999 appertaining to plot no. 1426, Khata No. 91, Mouza- Govindpur measuring an area of 6.45 acres out of total area of 8.37 acres registered in the name of the petitioner's mother-Late Kunti Devi as well as plot no. 1384, Khata no. 91 measuring an area of 3.31 acres out of total area of 5.85 acres registered in the name of petitioner's father- Late Bandhu Mahto.

(ii) For issuance of direction upon the respondent no. 5 to send the appropriate report to the respondent-CCL with respect to the aforesaid piece of lands for determining the compensation in terms with the Act, 2013 although the said lands were acquired in the year 1990 and the proceeding for which was initiated in the year Surendra Prasad Mahto vs M/S Central Coalfields Limited on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2096195/
1 2016.

entities.text: Surendra Prasad Mahto vs M/S Central Coalfields Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) For issuance of direction upon the respondent-CCL to extend benefits to the eligible family members of the petitioner in terms with the rehabilitation policy.

2. After some argument, learned counsel for the petitioner prays for withdrawal of the present writ petition with liberty to the petitioner to take other recourses available under law for redressal of his grievance.
3. Considering the said prayer of learned counsel for the petitioner, the writ petition is dismissed as withdrawn with aforesaid liberty.
4. I.A. No. 7896 of 2023 also stands dismissed accordingly.

(Rajesh Shankar, J.) Ritesh/
